atAGlance: Chè Thái is a fruit-and-jelly dessert with coconut milk, often durian, jackfruit, longan, lychee, and colorful jellies. It is creamy, fragrant, and loud in a good way.
whatItIs: Chè Thái is a rich fruit chè inspired by Thai-style dessert flavors, with coconut milk and mixed tropical fruit or jellies.
howToEnjoy: Stir enough to chill the coconut milk, then take small spoonfuls so the fruit and jelly textures stay distinct.
howLocalsOrder: Order chè thái cold and ask whether durian is included. Ask for less sugar if you want the fruit, jelly, and coconut milk to taste fresher.
worthKnowing: In Vietnam’s chè shops, Chè Thái is one of the more dessert-like cups: creamy, fruity, icy, and sometimes durian-forward, with texture doing as much work as sweetness.
goodToKnow: Ask about durian if the aroma worries you. Some cups include it by default; others keep it optional.
travelerCaution: May contain durian and dairy-style additions depending on the shop.
